title: Acute chest pain
priority: Second most common ED reason for visit in NHAMCS fact sheets.

layer0.label: Complaint
layer0.detail: Pain, pressure, tightness or discomfort in the chest, shoulders, arms, neck, back, upper abdomen or jaw; shortness of breath and fatigue count as equivalents.

layer0.label: History
layer0.detail: Pain characteristics, accompanying symptoms and cardiac risk factors.

layer0.label: Vitals and exam
layer0.detail: Sweating and fast breathing lean toward ACS, fast heart rate and dyspnea toward PE, air under the skin toward esophageal rupture; chest wall tenderness or pain on inspiration leans noncardiac.

layer0.label: 12-lead ECG
layer0.detail: Recorded and read within 10 minutes of arrival.

gate.label: Unstable or ECG emergency
gate.detail: Ongoing ischemic discomfort, dynamic ECG change, hemodynamic instability or serious arrhythmia: emergency escalation.

gate.label: Stable, ECG non-diagnostic
gate.detail: Work through the hypotheses, must-not-miss first, with serial high-sensitivity troponin.

gate_note: One normal ECG or one early troponin does not rule out ACS; patient characteristics must not be used to dismiss the complaint.

hypotheses.name: Aortic dissection
hypotheses.clue: Abrupt, tearing pain; pulse or BP differential

hypotheses.name: Common noncardiac causes
hypotheses.clue: Chest wall tenderness, pain on inspiration

steps.title: Focused history and exam
steps.description: Sets pre-test probability and picks the hypotheses to chase.

acs.text: Sweating and fast breathing raise suspicion.

pe.text: Fast heart rate and dyspnea raise suspicion.

ad.text: Abrupt, severe or tearing pain, pulse or BP differential, perfusion deficit.

ptx.text: Dyspnea, pain on inspiration, absent breath sounds on one side.

pna.text: Fever, localized pleuritic pain, dullness to percussion.

pc.text: Pleuritic, positional pain easing when leaning forward; friction rub.

nc.text: Chest wall tenderness or pain on inspiration points here.

steps.title: 12-lead ECG
steps.description: Best initial test; triggers the emergency pathway when ischemic.

acs.text: Ischemic or dynamic change escalates; one normal ECG does not rule ACS out.

pc.text: New widespread ST elevation or PR depression counts toward the two-of-four criteria.

steps.title: Chest radiograph
steps.description: Class 1 recommendation to look for other cardiac, pulmonary and thoracic causes.

ptx.text: Normal film with distress, pleuritic pain and hypoxia excludes it; absent vascular markings is diagnostic.

pna.text: Infiltrate or consolidation confirms; a normal film makes it unlikely.

pe.text: Often normal; with other causes excluded, a normal film raises PE probability.

ad.text: Mediastinal widening helps, but a film cannot rule out aortic syndromes at low probability.

pc.text: Recommended but does not establish the diagnosis.

steps.title: Serial high-sensitivity troponin and risk class
steps.description: Feeds the clinical decision pathway (low, intermediate, high risk).

acs.text: Low-risk class with non-ischemic ECG and negative serial troponin: no further acute testing.

pc.text: Recommended in suspected pericarditis but not diagnostic.

steps.title: Pre-test scoring of what is left
steps.timing: In parallel, for open must-not-miss causes
steps.description: A validated score sets the probability band that selects the next test.

pe.text: Wells two-level score; PERC first if suspicion is very low.

ad.text: ADD-RS 0 to 3: above 1 goes straight to imaging, 1 or less to D-dimer.

evidence.text: PE incidence is about 12% in the Wells unlikely band and about 37% in the likely band.
About 95% of patients with acute aortic dissection score intermediate or high on ADD-RS.
Meta-analysis: ADD-RS of 1 or more is about 94% sensitive alone and close to 100% with D-dimer; the best threshold depends on setting.

steps.title: D-dimer
steps.timing: Only at low or intermediate probability

pe.text: Wells 4 or less and D-dimer below the age-adjusted cutoff.

ad.text: ADD-RS 1 or less and D-dimer below 500 ng/mL (FEU): consider stopping; not externally validated.

steps.title: Definitive imaging for what remains
steps.description: Settles what earlier steps could not.

pe.text: CT pulmonary angiography: positive confirms, negative excludes.

ad.text: ECG-gated contrast CT from neck to pelvis is the recommended first-line imaging.

pc.text: Echocardiography: new or worsening effusion counts toward criteria.

evidence.text: ESC 2024 recommends a multiparametric diagnostic algorithm using ADD-RS (class I, level B).

steps.title: If the dangerous causes are eliminated
steps.description: Noncardiac causes become the working diagnosis.

nc.text: Chest wall pain, reflux esophagitis and costochondritis are most common in primary care.

acs.text: Low-risk patients do not need urgent stress testing or imaging.

eliminate_when.text: Low-risk class on the clinical decision pathway: non-ischemic ECG and negative serial high-sensitivity troponin.
Low-risk patients gain nothing from stress testing or imaging within 30 days.

do_not_rely.text: One normal ECG or one early troponin.
Dismissing the complaint because of sex, age, race, language or anxiety history.
Assuming acute troponin is available everywhere.

pe.validation: Secondary summaries of ESC and NICE; verify against originals.

eliminate_when.text: Very low suspicion and all eight PERC criteria met.
Wells 4 or less and D-dimer below the age-adjusted cutoff.

do_not_rely.text: D-dimer when clinical probability is high.
The standard Wells route in unstable or pregnant patients.

ad.validation: ESC 2024 recommends an ADD-RS-based diagnostic algorithm (class I, level B); MDCalc notes ADD-RS plus D-dimer lacks external validation.

eliminate_when.text: ADD-RS 1 or less and D-dimer below 500 ng/mL (FEU): consider stopping the work-up.
In ADvISED this strategy missed about 0.3% of acute aortic syndromes.
In the later PROFUNDUS study, ADD-RS 1 or less with negative D-dimer had a 0.2% failure rate.
Negative ECG-gated contrast CT, the first-line imaging in ESC 2024 (class I, level C).

do_not_rely.text: A D-dimer threshold in the wrong units (assumes FEU).

eliminate_when.text: Normal chest radiograph with respiratory distress, pleuritic pain and hypoxia.
Normal chest radiograph makes it unlikely, not impossible.

pc.validation: Diagnostic criteria only; no exclusion rule found.

do_not_rely.text: A normal ECG: without ST elevation the diagnosis is easily missed.
Chest film, markers or troponin as diagnostic; only ECG and echo help establish it.

pc.no_rule_note: No formal exclusion rule found. Diagnosis needs at least two of four criteria.

nc.no_rule_note: Not eliminated; it is what remains.

gaps.title: Local resources
gaps.text: Some sites cannot run acute troponin, so the pathway cannot be applied as written.

gaps.title: Which PE score
gaps.text: Wells, revised Geneva and YEARS lead to the same next steps, but protocols differ.

gaps.title: US versus Europe on dissection
gaps.text: ESC 2024 sends ADD-RS 2 or more to CT regardless of D-dimer; AHA guidance lacks consensus on the ADD-RS cut-off and on D-dimer.

gaps.title: Parallel hypotheses
gaps.text: No source found on prioritizing ACS, PE and dissection work-ups run at the same time.
